summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expands the direct public-company universe around the nuclear-fuel and execution bottleneck. The strongest direct exposure appears in HALEU enrichment, UF6 conversion, advanced fuel fabrication, and EPC/project-execution capacity rather than only in headline reactor developers. Two lanes are retained: reference names that define the node and an underfollowed discovery lane where nuclear exposure is embedded in specialty materials or diversified engineering labels. Layer 1B expansion for the nuclear-fuel/components/EPC chokepoint found a two-lane universe: reference names with already visible nuclear scarcity exposure, and underfollowed/speculative suppliers one or two steps away from headline reactor developers. The highest-evidence scarcity exposures are Centrus Energy for U.S. HALEU/enrichment and BWX Technologies for nuclear fuel/components and defense enrichment infrastructure. The underfollowed discovery lane is Mirion Technologies, a radiation-monitoring/instrumentation provider embedded in nuclear safety, compliance, SMR, and reactor-lifecycle workflows. ASP Isotopes is included only as a speculative shadow candidate because it has announced HALEU-related TerraPower agreements, but commercial uranium-enrichment capability, financing, licensing, and scale-up require verification. Expanded the US-listed universe for the nuclear fuel, HALEU, qualified-component, and execution-capacity node. The strongest direct public-market HALEU exposure remains Centrus Energy as a reference anchor, but the underfollowed discovery lane points to qualified nuclear components,
